10.1002_smll.75805: Electrochemical random‐access memory (ECRAM) enables analog conductance modulation by tuning the carrier concentration in the channel, making it a promising hardware platform for neuromorphic computing. Consequently, elucidating the quantitative relationship between the concentration of ionic defects and the conductivity of the channel material is essential for understanding the synaptic behavior of ECRAMs, which is still largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we employ La 0.6 Sr 0.4 FeO 3−δ (LSF) as a model system to quantitatively correlate the applied electrochemical driving force, ionic defect concentration, and modulated electrical conductance. Leveraging this correlation, we fabricate LSF‐based ECRAMs with high linearity, symmetry, and stable retention. To better understand the underlying principles in the electronic structures of LSF tuned by ionic defects, we further use operando ambient‐pressure x‐ray photoemission spectroscopy (AP‐XPS) to show that the evolution of conductivity and the shift of the Fermi level occur in high synchronization during conductance modulation. We show that defect chemistry offers a powerful theoretical basis for understanding and predicting the dynamic behavior and informs the rational design of device‐level engineering strategies of ECRAMs.
10.1016_j.jmrt.2026.09.051: This study investigates the combined influence of power supply mode and current density on PEO coatings produced in a fixed silicate-phosphate electrolyte. The coatings were produced in a silicate-phosphate-based electrolyte under conventional direct current (DC) conditions and under waveform-modulated DC mode using an external waveform generator (WG) at varying current densities. The results demonstrate that waveform modulation generally increased coating thickness and reduced surface roughness at low and intermediate current densities. The lowest surface porosity was obtained for J3 at 0.1 A·cm -2 . Surface and cross-sectional analyses revealed a more uniform microstructure with reduced pore density in waveform-controlled coatings. Corrosion performance was evaluated in Hank's solution using electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) for 168 h and potentiodynamic polarization (PDP) for 1 h. EIS measurements showed that the beneficial effect of waveform modulation depended on the applied current density, whereas PDP measurements demonstrated lower corrosion current densities for all waveform.modulated coatings. The enhanced corrosion resistance is attributed to the formation of a denser barrier layer and reduced electrolyte penetration pathways. These findings highlight the critical role of power supply mode, in conjunction with electrolyte chemistry and current density, in tailoring the morphology and corrosion performance of PEO coatings on magnesium alloys.
10.1021_acsnano.6c10656: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and cost-effective platform for electrochemical energy storage, yet their practical operation remains limited by water-driven parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous Zn deposition. Here, we report a molecule-crowding strategy that programs zinc/sodium trifluoroacetate (Zn(TFA)2/NaTFA) aqueous electrolytes into an anion-rich nanoclustered solvation environment. The balanced affinity of TFA– toward Zn2+ and H2O promotes Zn2+–TFA– association and drives the evolution from water-rich local coordination toward abundant contact ion pairs, ion aggregates, and interconnected multi-ion nanoclusters. Spectroscopic characterization, X-ray scattering, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal reconstructed Zn2+ coordination, extended ion-associated correlations, and reorganization of the water hydrogen-bonding environment, accompanied by reduced water activity. The nanocluster electrolyte suppresses hydrogen evolution and Zn corrosion and promotes more uniform Zn deposition. The optimized nanocluster electrolyte sustains Zn||Zn cycling for over 2100 h, enables Zn||Cu cells to operate for more than 3000 h with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.4%, and affords Zn||Na2V6O16·3H2O full cells with 82.4% capacity retention after 30,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. These results show that balanced anion interactions and molecular crowding regulate ion association and the water hydrogen-bonding environment, contributing to improved Zn reversibility and cycling stability.
